run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Hotel Reservation
Namespace: hotel-reservation

A hotel reservation application built with Go and gRPC, providing backend in-memory and persistent databases, a recommender system for hotel recommendations, and a functionality to place reservations.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The hotel-reservation application itself appeared healthy in the observable window: all 20 pods in namespace hotel-reservation were Running/Ready with 0 restarts at query time, every application Service Endpoints object had a ready address, application pod logs contained no runtime error lines, and the sampled frontend traces at 2026-11-23T23:30:34Z returned HTTP 200 for GET /hotels and GET /recommendations with fast child spans for search, geo, rate, profile, recommendation and reservation. The one component demonstrably failing is the auxiliary cleanup-controller: pod cleanup-controller-785f8c5b5b-9cgh7 repeatedly logs 'ConfigMap reservation-cleanup-token is Terminating; attempting controller-owned cleanup' followed by 'cleanup-controller reconciliation failed: Kubernetes API denied cleanup request with HTTP 403 Forbidden' (observed 23:30:23Z-23:30:33Z inside the authorized window, with 70 further such lines after the window through 23:31:44Z). ConfigMap reservation-cleanup-token carries deletionTimestamp 2026-11-23T23:30:22Z and finalizer cleanup.reservations.io/pending-cleanup, so it never finishes deleting. The denial is explained by the RBAC the controller runs under: Deployment cleanup-controller uses ServiceAccount cleanup-controller, bound by ClusterRoleBinding configmap-cleanup-controller to ClusterRole configmap-cleanup-controller, whose only rule grants get, list and watch on configmaps - no patch or update. That ClusterRole is where the fault originates. Separately, fault-injection scripts are staged in the environment: ConfigMaps failure-admin-geo and failure-admin-rate (scripts that revoke the MongoDB admin user's readWrite role on geo-db / rate-db and drop the admin user) are mounted at /scripts into the mongodb-geo and mongodb-rate Deployments, which were patched by kubectl-patch at 23:30:04Z. No execution of those scripts and no resulting DB authorization failure is visible in the window (mongod logs show successful admin authentication through 23:30:34Z and geo/rate spans were error-free), so that remains an unverified candidate rather than the concluded cause. Metrics history is essentially unavailable (the only Prometheus sample in the 24h window is at its very end), so no error-rate or latency trend could be established, and no application-level impact of the stuck ConfigMap was observed.

claims.text: Pod cleanup-controller-785f8c5b5b-9cgh7 in namespace hotel-reservation repeatedly logs 'ConfigMap reservation-cleanup-token is Terminating; attempting controller-owned cleanup' followed by 'cleanup-controller reconciliation failed: Kubernetes API denied cleanup request with HTTP 403 Forbidden' at 23:30:23Z, 23:30:25Z, 23:30:27Z, 23:30:29Z, 23:30:31Z and 23:30:33Z, and the same stream continues past the window (70 lines after 23:30:35Z, read through 23:31:44Z).

ConfigMap reservation-cleanup-token in namespace hotel-reservation is stuck deleting: it has metadata.deletionTimestamp 2026-11-23T23:30:22Z, finalizer cleanup.reservations.io/pending-cleanup, and label app.kubernetes.io/component=reservation-cleanup; its data is a redacted cleanup-token plus source=reservation-maintenance.

ClusterRole configmap-cleanup-controller contains exactly one rule: apiGroups [""], resources ["configmaps"], verbs ["get","list","watch"] - it grants no patch or update verb, so the controller's finalizer-removal PATCH on a ConfigMap cannot be authorized.

ClusterRoleBinding configmap-cleanup-controller binds ClusterRole configmap-cleanup-controller to ServiceAccount cleanup-controller in namespace hotel-reservation, and Deployment cleanup-controller runs with spec.template.spec.serviceAccountName=cleanup-controller executing 'python /controller/controller.py' from ConfigMap cleanup-controller-script.

The failing cleanup-controller is the only object in hotel-reservation observed producing error output: all 20 pods in the namespace were phase Running with ready=true and restartCount 0, and the cleanup-controller container has no previous (crashed) instance.

Application connectivity looked healthy in the window: every Service Endpoints object for the app (consul, frontend, geo, profile, rate, recommendation, reservation, search, user, memcached-*, mongodb-*) had exactly one ready address and no notReadyAddresses.

Sampled frontend traces at 2026-11-23T23:30:34Z are successful and fast: HTTP GET /hotels returned http.status_code=200 (e.g. 5148us, 4758us, 4398us) and HTTP GET /recommendations returned 200, with child spans /search.Search/Nearby, /geo.Geo/Nearby, /rate.Rate/GetRates, /profile.Profile/GetProfiles, /recommendation.Recommendation/GetRecommendations and /reservation.Reservation/CheckAvailability carrying no error status.

Reservation pod reservation-7d77c6cb59-jq7gr logged a clean startup: 'New session successfull...' against mongodb-reservation:27017 at 23:30:15Z, memcached-reserve client initialization, Consul agent initialization, 'Starting server...' and 'Successfully registered in consul' for srv-reservation at 10.244.234.157:8087 - with no error-level line in that stream.

Fault-injection assets are staged for the MongoDB-backed services: ConfigMaps failure-admin-geo and failure-admin-rate hold scripts that revoke the admin user's readWrite role on geo-db / rate-db and drop the admin user, and Deployments mongodb-geo and mongodb-rate mount them as volume failure-script at /scripts (ReplicaSet mongodb-geo-5ff578bcb8 template revision 2 has the extra volume; revision 1 ReplicaSet mongodb-geo-78487c9767 has none).

Deployments mongodb-geo and mongodb-rate are each at metadata.generation 2 and show a kubectl-patch write at 2026-11-23T23:30:04Z after their initial kubectl-client-side-apply at 23:30:03Z/23:30:04Z; every other application Deployment is at generation 1 created by kubectl-client-side-apply only.

Both MongoDB instances that have the injected scripts mounted were still authenticating the application's admin user normally in the window: mongodb-geo logged 'Authentication succeeded' for principalName admin from 10.244.7.244 at 23:30:13Z and mongodb-rate for principalName admin from 10.244.234.181 at 23:30:14Z and again at 23:30:34Z, with no 'not authorized' or authorization failure lines.

Cluster events in the authorized window contain no Evicted, OOMKilled, BackOff, Failed or Unhealthy event for the application: the hotel-reservation groups are Deployment ScalingReplicaSet (24), Pod Created/Pulled/Started/Scheduled (20 each), ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate (22) and SuccessfulDelete (2), plus PVC provisioning; the only 'Unhealthy' event is one Pod in namespace observe.

Prometheus has essentially no history for this window: count(up) returned a single sample of 93 series only at 2026-11-23T23:30:35Z, and a {__name__=~".+"} listing over 2026-11-23T22:30:35Z-23:30:35Z returned only cAdvisor, node-exporter, kube-state-metrics, Prometheus and go/process metrics - no application RED metrics - so no error-rate or latency baseline exists to compare against.

Against a MongoDB-privilege cause for any current application failure: the geo DB and rate DB servers logged successful admin authentications through 23:30:34Z, all mongodb-* Endpoints were ready, and the geo/rate/dependent spans sampled at 23:30:34Z were error-free - so no geo-db or rate-db authorization failure is observed in the authorized window.

Most likely mechanism for the observed 403 loop: because ClusterRole configmap-cleanup-controller lacks patch/update on configmaps, the cleanup-controller can never remove finalizer cleanup.reservations.io/pending-cleanup from ConfigMap reservation-cleanup-token, so that object stays in Terminating indefinitely and the controller retries and fails every 2 seconds.

Alternative, unverified candidate cause: the staged failure-admin-geo / failure-admin-rate scripts mounted at /scripts in mongodb-geo and mongodb-rate could have been (or could be) executed to revoke the admin readWrite role on geo-db/rate-db, which would break the geo and rate services on cache misses and propagate to search and frontend. No execution of those scripts, and no resulting authorization error, is visible in the authorized window, so this remains a candidate rather than a confirmation.

The stuck ConfigMap may not affect the reservation path at all: no Deployment in hotel-reservation references ConfigMap reservation-cleanup-token via volume, env valueFrom or envFrom (the only env valueFrom / envFrom query on the 20 Deployments returned empty lists), so the observable consequence is limited to the cleanup-controller failing and the ConfigMap never finishing deletion.

Rejected: the simultaneous creation of all 20 pods and the 2 ReplicaSet SuccessfulDelete events are not pod damage. There are no Evicted/OOMKilled/BackOff/Failed events, restartCount is 0 everywhere, and the two deleted ReplicaSets belong to the intentional kubectl-patch rollouts of mongodb-geo and mongodb-rate at 23:30:04Z - this is environment setup / rollout, not an incident.

Rejected as the incident cause: the frontend's 'grpc/lb/consul: error retrieving instances from Consul: ... connect: connection refused' lines. They occur only at 23:30:05Z-23:30:06Z while Consul was still starting, and shortly afterwards all Consul-backed Endpoints were ready and the sampled frontend requests returned HTTP 200 - a startup transient, not an ongoing failure.

Grant the cleanup-controller the verb it needs: add patch (and update) on configmaps to ClusterRole configmap-cleanup-controller, or bind an appropriately scoped Role/RoleBinding in hotel-reservation, then confirm the cleanup-controller logs its 'cleanup completed' line and ConfigMap reservation-cleanup-token disappears.

Confirm whether finalizer cleanup.reservations.io/pending-cleanup is still required on reservation-cleanup-token; if the cleanup work is done, remove the finalizer from the ConfigMap (owner-approved) instead of only widening RBAC, and review why the token ConfigMap is being deleted so shortly after creation.

Verify whether the revoke-admin scripts in failure-admin-geo / failure-admin-rate were actually executed against geo-db and rate-db, and remove the failure-script volumes from the mongodb-geo and mongodb-rate pod templates if they are not needed, so injection tooling is not left mounted in production pods.

gaps: No metrics history: count(up) had one sample (93 series) only at 2026-11-23T23:30:35Z and the metric-name listing for 2026-11-23T22:30:35Z-23:30:35Z contained only cAdvisor/node-exporter/kube-state-metrics/Prometheus/go/process series, so error-rate, latency and saturation trends (including whether application ERROR series exist at all) are unknown rather than zero.

The authorized window ends at 2026-11-23T23:30:35Z while the workloads started ~23:30:03Z-23:30:18Z; logs and traces after the window cannot be read (fetch_pod_logs dropped 70 cleanup-controller lines and 1-2 mongod lines after the window), so whether geo/rate began failing on MongoDB authorization after 23:30:34Z is unknown.

No evidence that the failure-admin-geo / failure-admin-rate revoke or drop-user scripts were executed (no exec or audit trail is available and the change_history integration is not configured), so the MongoDB privilege-revocation candidate cannot be confirmed or excluded.
The value of the reservation-cleanup-token 'cleanup-token' is redacted by the tools and could not be read, so any conclusion depending on it is unverified.

No consumer of ConfigMap reservation-cleanup-token was found among hotel-reservation Deployments; whether any out-of-namespace component reads it, and therefore whether the stuck deletion has functional impact, is unknown.
Application write operations were not exercised in the sampled traces - only Reservation/CheckAvailability appears - so failure of the place-reservation write path cannot be assessed.

The namespace contains no Role/RoleBinding objects; the only authorization for cleanup-controller was found at cluster scope (ClusterRole/ClusterRoleBinding configmap-cleanup-controller), and no API-server audit log is available to show which actor set the deletionTimestamp on the ConfigMap.

Several queries returned no matching data and therefore support no fact: traces_search_by_tags with error=true for frontend, reservation, geo, rate, search, user, recommendation and profile, and for frontend http.status_code="500"; the per-pod error-regex log reads for reservation, user, search, recommendation and profile; and the traces_* metric queries - these are unchecked/empty results, not evidence of health.
The resource-series query for traces_span_metrics_calls_total over 24h and the traces_* metric-name lookup returned no data, so span-level error counts per service are unknown.
The read of the saved frontend trace view was truncated (40 of 238 rows) and both sampled trace views are marked incomplete, so the trace evidence covers only a narrow slice at 2026-11-23T23:30:34Z.
next_steps: Add verbs patch/update on configmaps, scoped via a namespaced Role/RoleBinding for ServiceAccount cleanup-controller in hotel-reservation.

After the RBAC fix, confirm the cleanup-controller logs 'ConfigMap reservation-cleanup-token cleanup completed' and that the ConfigMap is gone; if the finalizer is no longer needed, remove it with owner approval.

Collect a fresh 24h of metrics, logs and traces outside the incident window to establish a baseline and check geo/rate MongoDB authorization errors ('not authorized on geo-db/rate-db') after 23:30:35Z.
Remove ConfigMaps failure-admin-geo and failure-admin-rate and their /scripts volume mounts from the mongodb-geo and mongodb-rate pod templates once the injection exercise is over.

{"controller.py":"import json
import os
import ssl
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

NAMESPACE = "hotel-reservation"
FINALIZER = "cleanup.reservations.io/pending-cleanup"
LABEL_SELECTOR = "app.kubernetes.io/component=reservation-cleanup"
TOKEN_FILE = [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] = "/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/ca.crt"
API_SERVER = (
    f"https://{os.environ['KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST']}:"
    f"{os.environ['KUBERNETES_SERVICE_PORT_HTTPS']}"
)
TLS_CONTEXT = ssl.create_default_context(cafile=CA_FILE)


def api_request(method, path, payload=None):
    data = None if payload is None else json.dumps(payload).encode()
    headers = [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]    if payload is not None:
        headers["Content-Type"] = "application/merge-patch+json"
    request = urllib.request.Request(
        f"{API_SERVER}{path}",
        data=data,
        headers=[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL],
        method=method,
    )
    with urllib.request.urlopen(request, context=TLS_CONTEXT, timeout=10) as response:
        raw = response.read()
        return json.loads(raw) if raw else {}


def reconcile():
    selector = urllib.parse.quote(LABEL_SELECTOR, safe="")
    response = api_request(
        "GET",
        f"/api/v1/namespaces/{NAMESPACE}/configmaps?labelSelector={selector}",
    )
    for configmap in response.get("items", []):
        metadata = configmap.get("metadata", {})
        finalizers = metadata.get("finalizers", [])
        if not metadata.get("deletionTimestamp") or FINALIZER not in finalizers:
            continue

        name = metadata["name"]
        remaining = [item for item in finalizers if item != FINALIZER]
        print(
            f"ConfigMap {name} is Terminating; attempting controller-owned cleanup",
            flush=True,
        )
        encoded_name = urllib.parse.quote(name, safe="")
        api_request(
            "PATCH",
            f"/api/v1/namespaces/{NAMESPACE}/configmaps/{encoded_name}",
            {"metadata": {"finalizers": remaining}},
        )
        print(f"ConfigMap {name} cleanup completed", flush=True)


print(f"cleanup-controller starting namespace={NAMESPACE}", flush=True)
while True:
    try:
        reconcile()
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
        if error.code == 403:
            print(
                "cleanup-controller reconciliation failed: "
                "Kubernetes API denied cleanup request with HTTP 403 Forbidden",
                flush=True,
            )
        else:
            print(
                f"cleanup-controller reconciliation failed: Kubernetes API returned HTTP {error.code}",
                flush=True,
            )
    except Exception as error:
        print(
            f"cleanup-controller reconciliation failed: {type(error).__name__}",
            flush=True,
        )
    time.sleep(2)
"}

{"k8s-geo-mongo.sh":"#!/bin/bash


ADMIN_USER="admin"
ADMIN_PWD="admin"

ROOT_USER="root"
ROOT_PWD="root"

TARGET_DB="geo-db"
READ_WRITE_ROLE="readWrite"

echo "Waiting for MongoDB to start..."
until mongo --eval "print('waited for connection')" > /dev/null 2>&1; do
  sleep 1
done
echo "MongoDB started"

# Create the admin user (will fail if the user already exists)
echo "Creating admin user..."
mongo admin --eval "db.createUser({user: '$ADMIN_USER', pwd: '$ADMIN_PWD', roles:[{role:'userAdminAnyDatabase',db:'admin'}]});"

# Grant readWrite role on the target database
echo "Granting readWrite role to $ADMIN_USER on $TARGET_DB database..."
mongo admin -u $ADMIN_USER -p $ADMIN_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.grantRolesToUser('$ADMIN_USER', [{role: '$READ_WRITE_ROLE', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"

# Create the root user (will fail if the user already exists)
echo "Creating root user..."
mongo admin --eval "db.createUser({user: '$ROOT_USER', pwd: '$ROOT_PWD', roles:[{role:'userAdminAnyDatabase',db:'admin'}]});"

# Grant readWrite role on the target database to root
echo "Granting readWrite role to $ROOT_USER on $TARGET_DB database..."
mongo admin -u $ROOT_USER -p $ROOT_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.grantRolesToUser('$ROOT_USER', [{role: '$READ_WRITE_ROLE', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"


echo "Initialization script completed"
"}
